reader.requirement: At --std 85, an indexed-file input-output statement that breaks the open-mode or operation-sequence rules, or a user-defined limit (the RECORD VARYING bounds), must be unsuccessful with a status whose first character is 4 (41-49), and must not take the INVALID KEY or AT END branch. The witness covers 41, 42, 43, 44 (WRITE short), 46 (after AT END), 47, 48 and 49 in sequential access, and dynamic 47, 48 and 49; it does not cover 46 after a failed START or random READ, READ on a never-opened file, REWRITE 49 in OUTPUT mode, or 44 on a long WRITE or a REWRITE.
reader.edition-search: grep CobolVersion|Edition|DialectBehavior over src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO. The hits are FileSharingFacility, CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector, IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly, IndexedReadPreviousAfterOpenAtEnd, RelativeWriteKeyOutOfRangeIsPermanentError and the report-writer switches. None is in the 41-49 guards (MutationOpenModeGuard, ReadOpenModeGuard, StartOpenModeGuard, the WRITE open-mode test, RecordRulesFailure). The USE tiers are edition-invariant by recorded determination (UseTierEmitter.cs header, kb/Work PB344).

reader.notes: Each logic-error guard runs before any key check or store change, and each answers a 4x status that the USE procedure sees. Neither INVALID KEY nor AT END is taken for a 4x status, as the IK-ST/IK-RD lines in p4le show. The path consults no edition, and 1985's text agrees with the later ones on these statuses.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:IX.1.3.4 GR5 and GRL2.5 (41-49) and the 1985 indexed Permissible Statements table (§1985:IX.4.4.4, lines 19196-19226). r2.cob at --std 85 (refute-1985-089/r2-001), probing the 43 and 46 arms the reader did not: sequential I-O REWRITE twice after one READ -> 43 with USE; DELETE after a successful START -> 43; REWRITE after a failed START (23) -> 43; DELETE after an AT END READ (10) -> 43; dynamic DELETE and two REWRITEs with no preceding READ -> 00 (43 is sequential-access only, as the text says); dynamic READ NEXT after AT END -> 46 and again 46, AT END not taken, and a random READ re-establishes position (00); dynamic OPEN INPUT DELETE 49, WRITE 48; OPEN OUTPUT START 47; second CLOSE 42. Each 4x ran the USE procedure and no INVALID KEY or AT END branch. Sequential-access WRITE in I-O mode (not permissible in 1985's table 2) answers 48; 48's text names I-O among the modes, so the code is the implementor's choice under 'If more than one value applies, the implementor determines', not a breach of GR5. grep DialectBehavior/Edition over FileConnector.cs, IndexedConnector.cs, KeyedConnector.cs: only FileSharingFacility (OPEN sharing), IndexedReadPreviousAfterOpenAtEnd and IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly, none on a 4x guard. cite.py: 'OK §1985:IX.1.3.4 GR5 (1.3.4 I-O Status) the text is in GR5'; 'OK §1985:IX.1.3.4 GRL2.5 (1.3.4 I-O Status) the text is in GRL2.5'.
